world.description: I, Pencil: a pencil supply chain that keeps running. Loggers cut cedar in Oregon, a mill saws it into slats, graphite is mined in Sri Lanka and mixed with clay into leads, a factory in Pennsylvania glues leads into slats, paints them and adds erasers and brass ferrules, packs them into boxes, and trucks deliver the boxes to shops across the country, which sell them to customers.

world.label: Pencil Supply Chain
world.summary: A recurring supply chain makes pencils from cedar, graphite, clay, and other materials and moves boxed pencils to shops and customers.

Pack pencils into boxes and add packed boxes to factory stock.
Carry packed pencil boxes from the factory to a shop in Pennsylvania.
Sell pencils from the shop to a customer for the listed unit price.

readout.title: How goods moved through the chain
readout.summary: The chain turned logs into slats and made leads and pencils, then packed some pencils and sold pencils to the customer. Logs, slats, leads, and graphite were delivered between businesses, while the factory made pencils using materials it already had in stock.

mechanisms.explanation: The lead-maker, logger, miner, and sawmill moved leads, logs, graphite, and slats to the next businesses in the chain.

mechanisms.name: Demand reached and met
mechanisms.explanation: The pencil shop sold pencils to the customer, whose pencil stock increased. The customer bought more pencils in later rounds too.
